I scanned the spec against the ambiguity taxonomy. It's unusually complete on behavior, exit codes, and edge cases — the real gaps are in how the store is stored and how strongly passwords are protected. I have a short queue of questions; here's the first.

**Question:** What one-way function should the tool use to protect stored passwords, and at what cost setting? (FR-026)

**Why it matters:** This decides how well the store resists an attacker who copies the file, and it also sets how long every `register`, `login`, `passwd` and `delete` takes — including the 50-run persistence test in SC-004, which runs the function 100+ times.

**Recommended:** Option A — `hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha256', ...)` at 600,000 iterations is the current OWASP guidance, is pure standard library with no OpenSSL feature requirements, and keeps the design to one function call (Principle IV). At roughly 0.2–0.3 s per call the full suite stays well inside a normal test run.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, 600,000 iterations, 16-byte random salt per account, constant-time comparison |
| B | `hashlib.scrypt` (memory-hard, n=2^14, r=8, p=1), stronger against GPU cracking, ~16 MB RAM per call |
| C | PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at a reduced 100,000 iterations, trading some margin for a visibly faster test suite |
| D | Single-pass salted SHA-256 — fastest, but offers almost no resistance to offline cracking (not recommended) |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (≤5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
